newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus leaders start talks in Nicosia.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus leaders start talks in Nicosia.

text.p: Greek and Turkish Cypriot community leaders met in Cyprus on Monday to try to resolve humanitarian issues associated with the conflict splitting their island.

The meeting between Cyprus President Glafcos Clerides, as head of the Greek Cypriot community, and Turkish Cypriot community leader Rauf Denktash took place at the residence of the United Nations resident envoy to Cyprus, Gustave Feissel.
Wearing a dark business suit, Clerides arrived at Feissel's residence first at 6.00 p.m. local, followed two minutes later by Denktash.
The two leaders emerged ten minutes later, where they gave a customary handshake in the presence of Feissel for cameras.
Asked what he expected from the meeting, Denktash replied: "Some beautiful cakes and some tea."
It is the first time the two leaders have met on home territory in nearly three years, although their offices are a five-minute drive away -- albeit cluttered with barbed wire.
Another two meetings are expected to follow.
Feissel's home is on the edge of the compound of what was once Nicosia airport. It became a U.N. protected zone after 1974.
The meeting was held two weeks after a series of U.N. sponsored talks in upstate New York aimed at reviving negotiations on establishing a bi-zonal, bi-communal federation on the island.
A second round of talks is tentatively scheduled to take place in Montreux, Switzerland, in mid August.
Cyprus has been virtually partitioned since troops from Turkey invaded the north of the island in 1974 in reaction to a Greek Cypriot coup in Nicosia engineered by the junta then ruling Greece.
The Turkish Cypriots proclaimed their own state in 1983 but it is recognised only by Ankara.

The Greek and Turkish Cypriots have been estranged since 1963, three years after independence from Britain, when a government representing both communities broke apart amid violence that resulted in the dispatch of a U.N. peacekeeping force that is still on the island.
